Definition: akin to G1099; sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine:--new wine.
BiblicalUsage: gleûkos is a plain word for new wine. In Acts 2:13, the text says "These men are full of new wine."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, gleûkos means new wine, and I leave it at that.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
